fix.note: Mexico: mud is usually 'el lodo'; barro is mostly clay. 'Los barros' = pimples.

ex.es: Los niños llegaron llenos de barro del parque.
ex.en: The kids came back from the park covered in mud.
Take off your shoes, they have mud on them.

ex.es: Compramos unas ollas de barro en el mercado.
ex.en: We bought some clay pots at the market.

fix.note: Feminine of el jefe. In Mexico, 'mi jefa' is also slang for 'my mom'.

ex.es: Mi jefa me dio el viernes libre.
ex.en: My boss gave me Friday off.

ex.es: La jefa de enfermeras habla español.
Mi jefa y mi jefe llevan treinta años casados.
ex.en: My mom and dad have been married for thirty years.

ex.es: Hay una gran brecha generacional entre mi abuelo y yo.
ex.en: There's a big generation gap between my grandpa and me.

ex.es: En mi empresa hay una brecha salarial entre hombres y mujeres.
ex.en: At my company there's a pay gap between men and women.

ex.es: Tomamos una brecha de tierra para llegar al pueblo.
ex.en: We took a dirt road to get to the town.

notes: Dropped Spain-only 'enhorabuena' (LatAm uses felicidades). Fixed barro note (Mexico mud = lodo), 'brecha' for a platform gap (unnatural), ambiguous 'mi jefa' = mom example.
